title: Monetary Policy and Economic Developments
summary: This Federal Reserve Annual Report excerpt reviews U.S. monetary policy and economic developments in 2018. The FOMC raised the federal funds rate target range twice in H2 2018, reaching 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent by December, before signaling a patient approach at the January 2019 meeting in light of softer global conditions and muted inflation. Economic activity grew at a solid pace with GDP rising under 3 percent for 2018, payrolls averaging 224,000/month, and unemployment near 4 percent, while PCE inflation declined to an estimated 1.7 percent by December.
key_points: FOMC raised federal funds rate target range twice in H2 2018, ending at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent following the December meeting
January 2019 FOMC meeting indicated patience in determining future rate adjustments amid softer global conditions and muted inflation pressures
Payroll employment growth remained strong at 224,000/month average since June 2018; unemployment averaged just under 4 percent
PCE inflation declined from slightly above 2 percent to an estimated 1.7 percent in December 2018; core PCE was 1.9 percent
Real GDP increased at a solid rate in H2 2018, rising a little under 3 percent for the full year
Financial conditions became less supportive of growth as risk appetite deteriorated late in 2018 amid trade tensions and global growth concerns
why_it_matters: This document provides the Federal Reserve's official retrospective assessment of 2018 monetary policy and economic conditions. The two rate hikes in H2 2018 marked a continuation of the gradual tightening cycle, while the January 2019 pivot to patience foreshadowed the eventual pause and subsequent easing cycle. The report documents the transition from solid growth and near-target inflation to growing concerns about global outlook and financial market volatility that characterized late 2018.
macro_context: The report documents a deceleration in global growth, particularly in the euro area and China, alongside trade tensions between the U.S. and China that weighed on financial market sentiment. Domestic economic conditions remained solid but showed signs of softening toward year-end, with business investment growth slowing and housing activity declining due to rising mortgage rates and input costs. The FOMC's pivot to patience in January 2019 reflected recognition of these headwinds.
market_structure_context: The report briefly addresses financial stability, noting the U.S. financial system remains substantially more resilient than pre-crisis levels, with historically high capital and liquidity ratios at large banks. However, it notes some deterioration in credit standards within segments focused on lower-rated firms, and elevated business debt levels.
important_numbers: 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent (federal funds rate target range by December 2018)
224,000 per month (average payroll employment growth since June 2018)
